cons: Validate maintenance, compatibility, and support requirements.
Validate maintenance, compatibility, and support requirements.
buyer_consensus.verdict: Choose Docker when the team prioritizes a widely documented Docker Desktop and Compose workflow across laptops. Choose Podman when daemonless operation, rootless-first workflows, pods, or alignment with a Red Hat container stack are concrete requirements. items.title: PostgreSQL vs SQLite for a production application backend
items.intent: Database decision brief

PostgreSQL.concurrency: Multiple concurrent readers and writers through MVCC
PostgreSQL.operations: Server deployment, upgrades, backups and monitoring
PostgreSQL.access: Native client connections over local or network transports
PostgreSQL.fit: Shared production systems and write-heavy multi-user services

SQLite.architecture: Embedded library operating on a local file
SQLite.concurrency: Many readers; write transactions are serialized
SQLite.operations: No server process; application owns file lifecycle and backups
SQLite.access: In-process API rather than a built-in network service
SQLite.fit: Local application state, edge workloads, prototypes and read-heavy services

buyer_consensus.status: No independently verified buyer-review dataset is available; technical synthesis only.
pros: A client-server relational database with network connections, server-managed concurrency, roles, extensions, and operational controls for multi-user applications.
An embedded SQL database delivered as a library, with a portable single-file format and no separate database server to operate.
cons: Server deployment, upgrades, backups and monitoring
No server process; application owns file lifecycle and backups
buyer_consensus.verdict: Choose SQLite when one application instance owns the data, deployment simplicity matters, and write concurrency is modest. Choose PostgreSQL when several processes or services write concurrently, clients connect over a network, or the team needs server-side access control and broader operational tooling.
